brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Something to keep sewing supplies tidy (a storage organizer)
requirements.evidence: Two adjacent hex bases (piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0) with a 3-compartment full-depth bin (bin:0,0,0) and a 2-compartment full-depth bin (bin:1,0,0). Open faces capped, joints bolted, check_build clean (meshClash clear, no issues).

requirements.requirement: Compartments suitable for sewing items (e.g. pins, buttons, bobbins, scissors)
requirements.evidence: Compartments exist (3 + 2). Only a pen (stood in the 3-compartment bin) and a steel ruler were placed as staging; a ruler placement timed out and the pencil did not seat in the 2-compartment bin, so the compartments are otherwise empty. Props are staging only; no sewing-specific tools exist in the catalog.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it does not assess the printed material. No lids were added, so dust protection is not provided.

finish.summary: Built a small two-cell organizer: a 3-compartment and a 2-compartment open-top bin on bonded hex bases, with open faces capped and joints bolted. The build passes check_build with a clear mesh check. A pen was staged in the 3-compartment bin for demonstration. The organizer is a fit-checked design only; material suitability and lids were not addressed.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
